extracted.intended_audience: PARI/GP users and C programmers integrating the PARI library (number theorists and advanced users writing GP scripts or library-mode programs)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference and how-to for writing GP scripts and for using PARI in C library mode, covering plotting primitives, control statements, GP-specific utility functions, memory/portability guidance, and object creation conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotrecth
rubrics_metrics.description: plotrecth(w, X = a, b, expr , {flag = 0}, {n = 0}): writes to rectwindow w the curve output of ploth(w, X = a, b, expr , flag, n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when you want the ploth curve drawn into a rectangular window w; semantics mirror ploth. No virtual cursor movement implied here (see related functions).

rubrics_metrics.name: plotrecthraw
rubrics_metrics.description: plotrecthraw(w, data, {flag = 0}): plot graph(s) for data in rectwindow w.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: data is a vector of vectors, each a list of coordinates. If parametric plotting is set use an even number of vectors where successive pairs are curves; otherwise first vector is x coordinates and others are y coordinates. flag has same significance as in ploth; recursive plot flag ignored.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotrline
rubrics_metrics.description: plotrline(w, dx, dy): draw in rectwindow w the part of the segment (x1,y1) - (x1+dx,y1+dy) which is inside w, where (x1,y1) is the current virtual cursor, and move the virtual cursor to (x1+dx,y1+dy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the portion inside w is drawn; virtual cursor always moves to the endpoint even if outside window.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotrmove
rubrics_metrics.description: plotrmove(w, dx, dy): move the virtual cursor of rectwindow w to position (x1+dx,y1+dy) where (x1,y1) is the initial cursor position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moves cursor relatively; does not draw.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotrpoint
rubrics_metrics.description: plotrpoint(w, dx, dy): draw the point (x1+dx,y1+dy) on rectwindow w if inside w, and move the virtual cursor to that position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draws a point only when inside the window; cursor moves regardless.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotscale
rubrics_metrics.description: plotscale(w, x1, x2, y1, y2): scale the local coordinates of rectwindow w so x runs from x1 to x2 and y from y1 to y2; x2<x1 and y2<y1 allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After plotinit default scaling is graphic pixel count and y axis points downwards; use plotscale whenever graphing functions to set desired coordinate conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotstring
rubrics_metrics.description: plotstring(w, x, {flag = 0}): draw on rectwindow w the String x at current cursor position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag selects justification: bits 1&2 for horizontal (0 left, 2 right, 1 center), bits 4&8 for vertical (0 bottom, 8 top, 4 v-center). Bits 16 and 32 insert small additional horizontal/vertical gap. See tutorial for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotterm
rubrics_metrics.description: plotterm(term): sets terminal where high resolution plots go (used currently by gnuplot driver); returns positive for success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With gnuplot driver possible terminals are same as gnuplot. If term='?' lists possible values. Terminal options and sizes can be appended to name as in 'gif=300,200'.

rubrics_metrics.name: psdraw
rubrics_metrics.description: psdraw(list): same as plotdraw but output is PostScript program appended to the psfile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to generate PostScript drawings rather than on-screen plots.

rubrics_metrics.name: psploth
rubrics_metrics.description: psploth(X = a, b, expr ): same as ploth except output is a PostScript program appended to psfile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For high-quality PostScript of function plots.

rubrics_metrics.name: psplothraw
rubrics_metrics.description: psplothraw(listx, listy): same as plothraw except output is PostScript appended to psfile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generate PostScript for raw list-based plots.

rubrics_metrics.name: break
rubrics_metrics.description: break({n = 1}): interrupts execution of current seq and immediately exits from the n innermost enclosing loops within the current function call (or top-level loop).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: n must be >= 1. If n greater than number of enclosing loops all are exited. Operates within same function call or top-level loop context.

rubrics_metrics.name: for
rubrics_metrics.description: for(X = a, b, seq): formal variable X goes from a to b and seq is evaluated; nothing done if a > b; a and b must be in R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard numeric loop; endpoint inclusion implied by syntax. Use when iterating over a numeric range.

rubrics_metrics.name: fordiv
rubrics_metrics.description: fordiv(n, X, seq): formal variable X ranges through positive divisors of integer n and seq is evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: n must be integer. Useful for divisor enumeration without manual factorization handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: forprime
rubrics_metrics.description: forprime(X = a, b, seq): X ranges over primes between a and b inclusive if endpoints are prime; nothing done if a > b; a and b must be in R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convenience loop to iterate prime numbers in an interval.

rubrics_metrics.name: forstep
rubrics_metrics.description: forstep(X = a, b, s, seq): X goes from a to b in increments s; nothing done if s>0 and a>b or s<0 and a<b; s must be in R* or a vector of steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If s is a vector [s1,...,sn], successive steps are used cyclically in order. Example given for non-uniform stepping.

rubrics_metrics.name: forsubgroup
rubrics_metrics.description: forsubgroup(H = G, {B}, seq): executes seq for each subgroup H of abelian group G (given in SNF or as vector of elementary divisors) whose index is bounded by bound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subgroups not ordered unless G is a p-group. Subgroups provided as generator matrices; intended for huge groups where listing all subgroups would be enormous. Example and canonicalization via mathnf shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: forvec
rubrics_metrics.description: forvec(X = v, seq, {flag = 0}): v is an n-component vector of two-component vectors [ai,bi]; seq evaluated with X[i] going from ai to bi. Highest index moves fastest. flag=1 generates nondecreasing vectors, flag=2 strictly increasing vectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for nested loops with variable bounds encoded compactly as vector of [ai,bi] pairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: if
rubrics_metrics.description: if(a, {seq1}, {seq2}): if a non-zero evaluate seq1 else seq2; seq1 or seq2 may be empty; boolean && and || short-circuit according to operator precedence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may omit second argument to get 'if (a, seq)'. Short-circuit evaluation makes constructs like 'if (reallydoit && longcomplicatedfunction(), ...)' safe.

rubrics_metrics.name: next
rubrics_metrics.description: next({n = 1}): interrupts execution of current seq and resumes next iteration of innermost enclosing loop within current function call (or top-level loop); if n specified resume at n-th enclosing loop; if n exceeds number of enclosing loops all are exited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous to C's continue but can target outer loops when given n>1.

rubrics_metrics.name: return
rubrics_metrics.description: return({x = 0}): returns from current subroutine with result x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard early exit from user-defined functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: until
rubrics_metrics.description: until(a, seq): evaluates seq until a is not zero. Condition tested after seq, so seq is always evaluated at least once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-tested loop; contrasts with while which pre-tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: while
rubrics_metrics.description: while(a, seq): while a is non-zero evaluate seq; test made before evaluating seq so if a initially zero seq never run.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-tested loop.

rubrics_metrics.name: addhelp
rubrics_metrics.description: addhelp(S, str): changes help message for symbol S; string str is expanded on the spot and stored as online help; if S is a user-defined function its definition is still printed before message str.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended to document global variables and user functions. You can overwrite help for built-ins but authors request feedback if you do.

rubrics_metrics.name: alias
rubrics_metrics.description: alias(newkey, key): defines keyword newkey as alias for keyword key; key must be existing function name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alias expansion happens immediately upon execution (fast). Intended for startup files (.gprc) to customize names; generally unnecessary in interactive use.

rubrics_metrics.name: allocatemem
rubrics_metrics.description: allocatemem({x = 0}): change PARI stack size after initialization; x must be non-negative integer; if x!=0 a new stack of size 16*(x/16) bytes allocated and data moved; if x=0 new stack is twice the old size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be the last instruction in any GP sequence because it usually moves the stack; it terminates by a longjmp rather than returning. Library variant is allocatemoremem(x) returning void.

rubrics_metrics.name: default
rubrics_metrics.description: default({key}, {val}, {flag}): sets default corresponding to keyword key to value val (val is a string). If val omitted prints current value. If flag set returns result instead of printing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typing default() prints the complete default list and current values. See sections referenced for available defaults and shortcuts.

rubrics_metrics.name: error
rubrics_metrics.description: error({str}*): outputs its argument list (each interpreted as string) then interrupts running GP program, returning to prompt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for signalling user-level errors; example 'error("n = ", n, " is not squarefree !")'. Automatic concatenation of strings allows single-argument usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: extern
rubrics_metrics.description: extern(str): runs external command named by string str and feeds its input into GP as if read from a file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UNIX-specific: use to invoke shell commands and import their output into GP.

rubrics_metrics.name: getheap
rubrics_metrics.description: getheap(): returns two-component row vector giving number of objects on heap and amount of memory they occupy in long words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mainly useful for debugging. Library syntax getheap().

rubrics_metrics.name: getrand
rubrics_metrics.description: getrand(): returns current value of random number seed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for debugging; library syntax getrand() returns C long.

rubrics_metrics.name: getstack
rubrics_metrics.description: getstack(): returns current value of top - avma, i.e. number of bytes used on stack; should be zero between commands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful mainly for debugging; library syntax getstack() returns C long.

rubrics_metrics.name: gettime
rubrics_metrics.description: gettime(): returns time in milliseconds elapsed since last call to gettime or start of containing GP instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for benchmarking or measuring elapsed time for blocks. Library syntax gettime() returns C long.

rubrics_metrics.name: global
rubrics_metrics.description: global({list of variables}): declares listed variables global; thereafter they cannot be used as formal parameters or loop indexes. Calling global with no args prints list of global variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps avoid accidental shadowing of globals in scripts; example shows danger with p used as both global and loop index and recommends declaring global at script start. eval(global) outputs values of all local variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: input
rubrics_metrics.description: input(): reads a string interpreted as a GP expression from input file (usually keyboard) and returns result of last expression in sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use print1 to prompt. Note quirks when using pari.el under Emacs: prompt must end with same prompt string as previous ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: install
rubrics_metrics.description: install(name, code, {gpname}, {lib}): loads from dynamic library lib the function name and assigns it gpname in GP session with argument code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for adding custom functions or accessing non-exported PARI library functions. Caution: may fail on statically linked systems causing segmentation fault; test on harmless examples first. Defaults: libpari.so and gpname=name when omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: kill
rubrics_metrics.description: kill(x): kills the present value of variable, alias or user-defined function x (only your own functions). Identifier can now be reused for other objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Killing a variable invalidates objects that used it; printing them will show funny placeholder. To restore variable to symbolic name use quote operator, e.g., a = 'a. Use kill to allow redefining variable as function or vice versa.

rubrics_metrics.name: print
rubrics_metrics.description: print({str}*): outputs string arguments in raw format ending with newline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic printing; print1 prints without trailing newline; printp and printp1 prettyprint with/without newline; printtex outputs in TeX format (useful for embedding in TeX manuscripts).

rubrics_metrics.name: print1
rubrics_metrics.description: print1({str}*): outputs string arguments in raw format without ending newline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for prompts when combined with input().

rubrics_metrics.name: printp
rubrics_metrics.description: printp({str}*): outputs string arguments in prettyprint (beautified) format ending with newline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for human-readable formatted output.

rubrics_metrics.name: printp1
rubrics_metrics.description: printp1({str}*): outputs string arguments in prettyprint format without ending newline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines prettyprint formatting with prompt-style behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: printtex
rubrics_metrics.description: printtex({str}*): outputs string arguments in TeX format to standard output so they can be used in TeX manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To send to a file, use writetex or enable log defaults; examples show default(logfile, 'new.tex'); default(log,1); printtex(result).

rubrics_metrics.name: quit
rubrics_metrics.description: quit(): exits GP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminate GP session; analogous to exit.

rubrics_metrics.name: read
rubrics_metrics.description: read({str}): reads in file whose name is expansion of str and evaluates it; if str omitted re-reads last file fed to GP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return value is result of last expression evaluated in file.

rubrics_metrics.name: reorder
rubrics_metrics.description: reorder({x = []}): if x is empty returns vector of existing variable names in increasing order of importance; if x non-empty must be permutation of variable names and gives new order for output only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Killed variables shown as 0. Example shows using reorder([z,x]) to change output precedence; internal representation unaffected.

rubrics_metrics.name: setrand
rubrics_metrics.description: setrand(n): reseeds random number generator to value n; initial seed is 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax setrand(n) returns n. Useful to control randomness for reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: system
rubrics_metrics.description: system(str): executes system command str, writes output to standard output (not to logfile), and returns control to PARI system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UNIX-only wrapper around C system command; useful for invoking shell utilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: trap
rubrics_metrics.description: trap({e}, {rec}, {seq}): tries to execute seq trapping error e and preventing it from aborting; if error occurs recovery sequence rec is executed and its evaluation becomes the result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If seq omitted defines default action rec when encountering e. If rec omitted a break loop is started where commands are read and evaluated until next/break/return. Useful for debugging long computations (e.g., after ^C). A list of named exceptions recognized is provided and will be expanded; examples given for division by zero handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: type (GP-only)
rubrics_metrics.description: type(x, {t}): under GP, if t absent returns internal type number of object x; if t present makes a copy of x and sets its type to t (number or symbolic name like t_FRACN).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GP ensures consistency of object internal structure; can create reducible rationals or rational functions by changing type. Library equivalents typ and settyp behave differently: settyp changes type in place and does not create a copy and does not check consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: whatnow
rubrics_metrics.description: whatnow(key): if key names a function present in GP version <=1.39.15 outputs new function name and syntax if it changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps users migrate code across GP versions; example notes that many functions changed names/syntax and this helps map old to new.

rubrics_metrics.name: write / write1 / writetex
rubrics_metrics.description: write(filename, {str}*): appends remaining arguments with newline to filename; write1 appends without trailing newline; writetex writes in TeX format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to persist output to files; writetex helpful for TeX-ready output.

rubrics_metrics.name: include_pari_h
rubrics_metrics.description: Include directive: #include <pari.h> to use PARI in C programs; pari.h imports necessary constants, macros, and defines the GEN type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the mandatory header to access PARI library functions and types when programming in library mode.

rubrics_metrics.name: pari_init
rubrics_metrics.description: void pari_init(long size, long maxprime): first executable statement in main program to initialize PARI system and PARI stack; size is bytes for PARI to work with, maxprime is upper limit on precomputed prime table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Size should not reasonably be below 500000. If many PARI functions require primes and you see 'not enough precomputed primes' increase maxprime. Use maxprime=2 if you don't want primes (but many functions need primes).

rubrics_metrics.name: PARI_stack_and_garbage_guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: PARI provides a large stack for computations and leaves garbage collection to the programmer: you must clean up intermediate results when not needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special purpose routines exist for cleanup; avoid relying on automatic GC to prevent performance slowdowns. Understand that PARI's memory model expects manual management of stack usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: universal_objects
rubrics_metrics.description: On initialization PARI provides universal objects: 2 (ghalf), integers 0,1,2 (gzero, gun, gdeux), fraction 1, complex i (gi), polynomials polx[v] and polun[v] for variable indices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polynomials for variables other than 0 and MAXVARN are not created on init; programmer must fill them before use (never by direct assignment). These universal objects live off-stack.

rubrics_metrics.name: heap_and_primes_table
rubrics_metrics.description: PARI has a heap of permanent universal objects and a table of primes (diffptr) used internally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmers rarely interact directly with heap; prime table usage described in appendices. Be aware functions rely on these structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: typecasts_and_macros_guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Due to PARI GEN representation many typecasts are necessary when programming in C; macros exist (paricast.h) to reduce casting, e.g., replacing leading 'g' by 'l' in function names for long casts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use provided macros like lpolx[v], ladd(x,y), maeln and gmaeln for multidimensional access. Be aware a cast is not a valid lvalue. Use coeff for matrices and mael otherwise. Familiarize with paricast.h to avoid tedious casts.

rubrics_metrics.name: variations_on_basic_functions and naming_conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Many basic PARI functions have variants (e.g., gaddgs, gaddsg, gaddz, gaddgsz, gaddsgz) for combinations of GEN and long arguments and for placing result into preexisting GEN to avoid stack growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Low-level specialized functions exist for specific types (addii, addrr, etc.). Using general g* functions is simpler and safer because types of intermediate results can vary; using specialized functions risks type mismatches. z-suffixed functions put result into preexisting GEN and avoid stack allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: portability_32_vs_64_bit
rubrics_metrics.description: PARI supports both 32-bit and 64-bit machines; header files and macros adapt but library compiled for one architecture only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use portable macros like BITS_IN_LONG, LONG_IS_64BIT, DEFAULTPREC, MEDDEFAULTPREC, BIGDEFAULTPREC. Be aware that prec arguments to functions like gexp produce different bit accuracies on 32 vs 64 bits; use conditional compilation to select appropriate prec values.

rubrics_metrics.name: bit_accuracy_formula
rubrics_metrics.description: bit_accuracy(prec) = (prec - 2) * BITS_IN_LONG; decimal digits are bit_accuracy * log(2)/log(10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: prec=5 gives ~28 decimal digits on 32-bit and ~57 on 64-bit machines. Adjust prec or use DEFAULTPREC macros for consistent precision across architectures.

rubrics_metrics.name: cgetg_cgeti_cgetr_object_creation
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN cgetg(long length, long type) creates a PARI object by allocating length longwords on the PARI stack and setting type; cgeti and cgetr are specialized for integer and real leaves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: length and type must be correct; function does not check lengths for many types, so misuse causes disasters. Use cgeti/cgetr for leaves. Macros lgetg/lgeti/lgetr return (long) values.

rubrics_metrics.name: predetermined_lengths_for_some_types
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain types have predetermined lengths: length 3 for t_INTMOD, t_FRAC, t_FRACN, t_COMPLEX, t_POLMOD, t_RFRAC, t_RFRACN; length 4 for t_QUAD, t_QFI; length 5 for t_PADIC, t_QFR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For efficiency no checking is done in cgetg, so supply correct lengths for these special types or risk memory corruption.

rubrics_metrics.name: examples_of_object_creation_and_usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: create integer object z = cgeti(DEFAULTPREC) or cgetg(DEFAULTPREC, t_INT); create complex with z=cgetg(3,t_COMPLEX); create 4x3 matrix by nested cgetg and lgetg calls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples demonstrate how to allocate objects and when to allocate columns/elements separately. Use MEDDEFAULTPREC for complex components when needed.
